summary: The starter prompt clearly defines the core goal: a Python LlamaIndex-based service that stores formulary entries with embeddings in Azure DocumentDB and exposes a /formulary-search endpoint returning the top-10 vector-similarity matches. Several operational details (embedding model/provider, exact Python/driver versions, index dimensions & parameter choices, seed data/source, README/run/test details, infra-as-code) are not specified and will be chosen by the builder or supplied by installed skills where applicable.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Python LlamaIndex service that stores drug formulary entries ... Expose a /formulary-search endpoint ... returns the top 10 formulary matches ranked by vector similarity."
rubric.note: Business problem, user and demonstration are clear from the prompt.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Build a standalone single-agent sample: a locally runnable Python web service (no multi-agent orchestration). Use a simple local development workflow.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't say whether to use any agent framework or multi-agent orchestration; builder will default to a simple app.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use a modern Python 3.x runtime (assume Python 3.11). Virtualenv will be used and pip installs will work as described in skill_md.
rubric.note: Python is required but no explicit version; skill_md indicates python/pip are available in a virtualenv.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the official pymongo driver and follow documentdb-driver guidance (e.g., pymongo >= 4.x).
rubric.note: The documentdb-driver skill covers recommended driver usage (singleton MongoClient etc.) though it doesn't mandate an exact version.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "This sample is being built on a developer machine where an Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned and reachable." and "use the database named `sample_healthcare_10`" (skill_md).
rubric.note: skill_md provides the target cluster details (vector-capable, compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol) and the database name to use.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "connection string is in the environment variable `DOCUMENTDB_URI`. Read it from the environment at run time." (skill_md)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Database connection string is read from DOCUMENTDB_URI; embedding/model credentials will be read from environment (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY or LLAMA_INDEX_API_KEY).
rubric.note: DB connection is specified to come from env var, but the prompt does not say where model API keys/credentials live.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "stores drug formulary entries (name, indications, contraindications, dosing) as DocumentDB documents with embedded vectors."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Single collection within sample_healthcare_10 (e.g., collection name `formulary`) with each document containing fields: name, indications, contraindications, dosing, embedding (vector array). No sharding by default.
rubric.note: Fields and embedding-in-document requirement are explicit. Shard key/partitioning not mentioned; builder will likely keep a single collection.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide a small synthetic seed dataset (dozens of entries) in JSON/CSV seeded by a script (e.g., scripts/seed_data.py). Use permissive licensing / synthetic content. Seed script is idempotent (upsert by unique drug name or _id).
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't describe source, size, license or how to load data; skill_md asks to load sample data but doesn't supply it.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a cosmosSearch vector index (e.g., vector-hnsw or vector-ivf/diskann) on the embedding field in code with similarity=cosine and dimensions matching the chosen embedding model's output.
rubric.note: Prompt asks for vector similarity search; documentdb-vector-search and documentdb-indexing cover index types and guidance. Exact index-creation-in-code and parameters will need choices from the builder.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use LlamaIndex with a hosted embedding provider (assume OpenAI text-embedding-3-small or another commonly used embedding model). Set corresponding API key in env (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY). Assume embedding vector dimension consistent with that model (e.g., 1536 for many OpenAI embeddings).
rubric.note: Prompt requires LlamaIndex but does not specify which embedding model/provider or dimensions.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Expose a /formulary-search endpoint that accepts a clinical intent description ... and returns the top 10 formulary matches"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Implement as an HTTP API endpoint (e.g., FastAPI) accepting POST JSON { "query": "..." } or form data.
rubric.note: Endpoint path and expected behavior (top 10 ranking) are explicit; input format and framework left to implementer.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Do not provide infrastructure-as-code for provisioning the cluster in this sample; sample will rely on the pre-existing cluster. If infra code were required, documentdb-azure-deployment skill could be used.
rubric.note: Starter prompt explicitly expects to use an existing cluster; reference's requirement to include infra-as-code is not satisfied by the prompt.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Include README with commands: pip install -r requirements.txt, export DOCUMENTDB_URI and model API key env vars, python scripts/seed_data.py, uvicorn main:app --reload, then curl POST to /formulary-search. Unit tests will be basic and some integration steps may require live cluster.
rubric.note: skill_md gives environment expectations but not explicit runnable commands or tests.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Accept when: seed script creates collection and vector index, sample data loaded, /formulary-search returns top-10 results for sample queries, and README documents how to run and verify.
rubric.note: No explicit acceptance criteria provided in the prompt.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Keep sample small and low-cost (do not demonstrate production HA/CMK/Private Endpoint). State that production security & scalability are out-of-scope.
rubric.note: No cost or compliance constraints were provided.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Never write its value into any file, log, README or test fixture; use a config file or `.env.example` with a placeholder, as the prompt asks." (skill_md)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a `.env.example` with placeholders (DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY, etc.), requirements.txt with pinned deps, a top-level README, scripts/seed_data.py, app/ or src/ folder for code.
rubric.note: skill_md instructs use of .env.example and env-driven configuration and the local-deployment skill covers repo/runtime conventions.

questions_for_author: Which embedding model and provider should LlamaIndex use (e.g., OpenAI text-embedding-3-small) and where should we read its API key from (env var name)? This determines vector dimensionality and index params.
Which Python version should the sample target (e.g., 3.10 or 3.11)?
Which web framework do you prefer (FastAPI, Flask)?
Do you want infrastructure-as-code for cluster provisioning included in the repo, or should the sample explicitly rely on the pre-provisioned cluster described in skill_md?
Do you require pinned dependency versions in requirements.txt and unit tests that run without a live cluster (using mocks)?
requirements_at_risk: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository. Reason: DOCUMENTDB_URI is specified in skill_md, but the prompt does not specify where embedding/model credentials live.
.env.example lists every setting with placeholder values. Reason: skill_md asks for a .env.example, but the prompt doesn't require listing every setting; builder may omit some env vars.
The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output. Reason: embedding model/provider not specified, so exact dimension is unknown and may not be enforced when creating the index.

The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one. Reason: prompt asks for vector search but doesn't require parameter choices or README guidance.

A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data. Reason: prompt asks to store documents and skill_md expects loading sample data, but no seed script spec is provided.
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails. Reason: error-handling behavior is not described in the prompt.
Search results include the similarity score. Reason: prompt requires ranking by similarity but does not explicitly require returning numeric similarity scores.
Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt. Reason: prompt says use Python but doesn't require pinned versions; skill_md notes pip works but not pinning.
Unit tests run without a live cluster. Reason: no testing strategy is provided; tests that mock DocumentDB would need to be added explicitly.
Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type. Reason: prompt expects use of an existing cluster and does not request infra-as-code.
